newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill market lures buyers after rates rise.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill market lures buyers after rates rise.

text.p: Manila's secondary Treasury bills market showed some life on Tuesday as buyers trickled in after interest rates rose in yesterday's auction, traders said.

"There was movement in the one-year bills. It's a good price to go in," a foreign bank dealer said, adding some banks were expecting a softening of rates next week when over six billion pesos would be flushed into the system following the reserve requirement cut.
"But the bad news is rates are still high," another trader said. "The market is convinced it is not liquidity-driven anymore."
The trader said rates could remain high even with the reserve requirment cut on July 4.
She said the money market is now determined by the development in the foreign exchange market. With the Central Bank keeping its key rate at 15 percent, there was still no urgency to buy T-bills.
A Reuters poll of eight financial institutions gave wide bids of 10.90/11.25 percent for the three-month bills; 11.375/11.60 percent for the six months; and 11.75/12 percent for the one-year bills.
The average interbank call loan rate stayed at 15.0625 percent, with 32 lenders and 22 borrowers.
Volume swelled to 28.68 billion pesos from 19.5 billion pesos as banks beefed up their positions for the first half book closing, dealers said.
Trades done today are valued the previous day, June 30.
